base_prompt_template: {SHOT}. Editorial luxury photography, museum-grade biennale-catalogue restraint, natural or single-source light, muted paper-and-ink palette with at most one small vermilion (#C93A1E) accent, shallow depth, film grain, no text, no logos, no people's faces, generous negative space, 16:9. Absolutely no satellites, rockets, spacecraft, solar panels, antennae, mission-control screens, planet-with-rings, orbit swooshes, star-field wallpaper, or sci-fi rendering; no musical notes, clefs, staves, soundwaves, or instruments; no premium black-and-gold; no generic tech-startup or dashboard look.

assets.shot: In the vacuum of open space: a matte-black robotic arm's gripper opens and releases a matte-white unbranded sneaker, which drifts free and tumbles weightlessly away. The sun blazes low and enormous behind the rig, its hard flare sweeping across the arm's joints as the shoe releases, then settling to reveal the sneaker sharp in macro focus against the blackness of space with the sun a brilliant point of light and faint stars visible.

assets.shot: A weathered, hand-modified vintage medium-format camera on a plain grey studio backdrop — hand-cut wooden gear-shaped discs bolted to its lens barrel, a small hairline vermilion painted disc marking, a fine metal ball-chain lanyard, hand-lettered serial numbers on the white-painted chassis. No brand names, no logos, no wordmarks, no agency insignia.
assets.note: Operator supplied a reference image (/Users/paulestevez_ipx_temp/Downloads/cosmos_324186223_16_9.png) of a similarly kit-bashed vintage camera prop carrying a visible NASA logo and NASA-red color scheme. Declined to use it directly or replicate the branding — real trademark exposure plus a direct violation of the deck's own hard line (no aerospace-agency association, ever). Regenerated the same weathered/hand-modified aesthetic with all insignia stripped and the accent recolored to Rhapsody vermilion (#C93A1E).

assets.shot: Extreme motion-blur streaks of light racing across a black void toward a thin luminous horizon line, where a planet's atmosphere glows faintly in muted blue-green at the edge of frame. Pure light and velocity, no visible spacecraft or hardware.
assets.note: Operator supplied a reference image (/Users/paulestevez_ipx_temp/Downloads/cosmos_134875125_16_9.png) of a literal satellite/spacecraft exterior (visible hull, radiator panels, mechanical hardware) racing over Earth's limb. Declined to use it or replicate the hardware — this is not a trademark issue like the Section 02 case, it's the exact category cliche the deck's entire premise exists to avoid (Spine hard line: no satellites, no spacecraft, no solar panels or antennae, ever). Kept only the kinetic motion-streak and atmospheric-glow mood, stripped of all mechanical/spacecraft content.
